title: Mock Test

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate idiom for the underlined part in the given sentence:
Sohan was very much perplexed to find that his younger brother Mohan had taken poison
questions.solution: B) At his wit’s end(idiom) – Very much perplexedअत्यधिकउलझनमें

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Yeoman’s service
questions.solution: A)Yeoman’s service(idiom) – Excellent work done उत्कृष्ट कार्य किया

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
The Government must strive to provide a/an fair and square deal to the citizen of its country.
questions.solution: B)fair and square(idiom) –honest and straightforwardईमानदार और सीधा

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
By leaps and bounds
questions.solution: D)By leaps and bounds(idiom) –Rapidlyतेज़ी से

questions.question:
Select the sentence that uses the given idiom correctly.
Skating on thin ice.
options: They were on thin ice when they skated on the frozen lake.
She was on thin ice while trying to balance on a tightrope.
He was on thin ice after making a controversial statement.
They were on thin ice due to the icy conditions on the road
questions.solution: C) Skating on thin ice (phrase) - in a precarious or risky situation.किसी अनिश्चित या जोखिम भरी स्थिति में।

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Be in seventh heaven
options: To be in a state of extreme happiness
To avoid talking about what’s important
questions.solution: C)Be in seventhheaven(idiom) – To be in a state of extreme happiness अत्यधिक खुशी में होना

questions.question:
Identify the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Bread and butter
questions.solution: B)Bread and butter(idiom) – Means of livelihoodरोज़ीरोटी

questions.question:
Based on the situation in the sentence, select the most appropriate idiom for the underlined segment.
After the Pandemic, his business crumbled and he is in a difficult situation.
questions.solution: D) Be in a tight corner(idiom) – In a difficult situation कठिन स्थिति में होना

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Ignoring his father’s warnings, he said, “an elephant in the room” to his mother.
options: The elephant got stuck in the room
questions.solution: B)An elephant in the room(idiom) – There is an obvious problem एक स्पष्ट समस्या

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence.
Only those having blue blood can dethrone the evil autocrat and restore equilibrium
questions.solution: C)Blue blood(idiom) – Aristocratic lineage शाही वंशावली

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Go down in flames
questions.solution: A)Go down in flames(idiom) – To fail spectacularly बड़ी असफलता

questions.question:
Select the phrase/idiom that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence.
After two hours of wandering in the desert, we realised we were on a wild horse race.
questions.solution: A)wild goose chase(phrase/idiom) – A futile or hopeless pursuit; an attempt to accomplish something that is ultimately unsuccessful निरर्थक या असफल प्रयास

questions.question:
Identify the meaning of the idiom in the given situation.
I will always stand by my friend
questions.solution: C)Support in difficult situation- "I will always stand by my friend" means to support them in difficult situations. सहायता करना मुश्किल परिस्थितियों में

questions.question:
Choose the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
At the drop of a hat
questions.solution: D)At the drop of a hat(idiom) – Immediately तुरंत

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
The players like the coach because he is honest, realistic and practical in dealing with them.
questions.solution: A)down to earth– realistic and practical यथार्थवादी और व्यावहारिक

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate idiom for the given situation focusing on the underlined words.
I invited them to my anniversary dinner but they had other plans, so they decided to politely decline with the implication that they may come at a later date
options: Took it with a grain of salt
questions.solution: B)To take a rain check(idiom) – To politely decline with the implication that they may come at a later date शिष्टाचारपूर्वक मना करना और बाद में आने का सुझाव देना

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Gift of the gab
options: A gift for a person named Gab
questions.solution: B)Gift of the gab(idiom) – A talent for speaking बोलने की प्रतिभा

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate idiomatic expression that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
He is very strict with his students but good-natured .
options: his eyes are bigger than his stomach
his heart is in the right place
questions.solution: B) His heart is in the right place(idiom) – good-natured अच्छे स्वभाव वाला

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
Popular cosmetics brands in India are very expensive
options: take it with a pinch of salt
cost an arm and a leg
questions.solution: D) cost an arm and a leg(idiom) – very expensive बहुत महंगा

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
To leave no stone unturned.
options: To win everything that is available
To do everything possible to achieve something
To treat someone/something as if of no importance
questions.solution: C)To leave no stone unturned(idiom) – To do everything possible to achieve something हरसंभव प्रयास करना
